text:
maria: re: model onboarding — quick thread to align on the prober matrix + gating contracts. had a 1:1 with infra and we need to decide interface boundaries before the next ship
alex: high level: we want a lightweight prober service that runs deterministic checks (load, output shape, perf) and an async heavy bencher that runs longer evals. prober should be required on ingest path.
kevin: agreed. main question: where to keep the gating policy? prober returns a structured report; should the gate decision live in model-registry or in the ingest lambda?
julia: leaning registry-side so we can version gate rules with the model and roll back. also makes audits easier.
maria: +1 on registry. registry can tag model as "probed:pass" / "probed:warn" / "probed:fail" and expose webhooks. ingest flow only needs to halt on fail.
alex: that means prober schema needs to be stable. proposed minimal schema: {status, checks: [{name, ok, value, threshold, note}], artifacts: [perf_trace_url], fingerprint}. we can compress the perf traces elsewhere.
kevin: sounds good. what about numeric thresholds? e.g., p95 latency < X ms depends on instance type. prober should report normalized metrics and raw numbers. gating rules can be functions of instance_class.
julia: example: gate rule: if instance_class in [g4dn, a10g] use latency thresholds A else use B. make it declarative so product can tweak.
maria: we already have bench-bot producing median p95s for previous models. bench-bot could seed default thresholds based on similar-arch baselines.
bench-bot: auto-report: found 3 prior int8 Llama2 variants with p95 120-180ms on a10g. recommending default p95 threshold = 220ms (safety margin). :robot_face:
alex: nice. another tradeoff: should prober do a tiny generation sample to validate logits/outputs vs expected fingerprint or only structural checks?
kevin: fingerprinting is useful to detect export/conversion errors. but exact tokens may vary due to FP math. we can use a hash of top-k logits pattern or K-L divergence to a golden. that is robust.
julia: agreed on KL/emd style divergence with a threshold. also check kv-cache shape and max sequence behavior.
maria: ops question: where to run the prober? Ingest path is synchronous, so prober must be async. We should enqueue a prober job, fail fast if export missing, but allow manual override for canaries.
alex: flow: upload -> registry registers model meta -> enqueue prober job -> prober writes report -> registry evaluates gate -> if fail block automatic deploy; manual override allowed with audit log.
kevin: what about large models taking hours to probe? need a fast-pass smoke + scheduled deep probe. fast-pass should run in <5m and cover: shape, quick perf with short seq len, fingerprint KL on 16 tokens, memory footprint. deep probe can run nightly for thorough benching.
\jmaria: typo: (maria) deep probe nightly makes sense. fast-pass thresholds stricter for shape/perf but looser for quality.
julia: UI implications: in Console show probe status + top failing checks + link to perf traces. also include a "re-run prober" button.
maria: security note: prober runs customer model blobs in infra — must respect private deployments and VPC policies. for private onboarding we run prober in customer VPC or in air-gapped runner.
alex: good call. add attribute prober.run_location -> {hosted, dedicated, vpc_runner}. gating rules to consult that.
kevin: implementation TODOs: 1) prober service API spec (openapi) 2) registry gating DSL + evaluator 3) fast-pass job image (small runner) 4) bencher for deep runs and threshold seeding.
maria: I'll draft the OpenAPI and a minimal prober payload today. can we agree the schema and the flow?
julia: yes, agreed. followups: I can mock a registry rule example and a Console prototype.
alex: I'll wire prober enqueue from ingest lambda and add webhook support. kevin handle the fingerprint comparator and KL calc.
kevin: will do. PRs up next week. small note: include a reason code taxonomy for failures so SRE / SEs can triage quickly (export error, perf-regression, mismatch, infra).
\jmaria: (maria) +1. also tag owner on the registry when a model fails so eng knows to look.
bench-bot: scheduled note: will run baseline seeding job tonight for int8 models and post suggested thresholds under /bench/seed. :alarm_clock: 
alex: ok team, I'll create the tracking ticket and add the API sketch. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
